meta.description: Canonical source bibliography. Every citable document referenced in fact sheets, case files, or research notes.
meta.schema: sourceId → {citation, archive, url, corpusStatus, corpusPath, mediaPath, validationPath, notes}

dg-rec-pt1.citation: Gurney, Daniel. The Record of the House of Gournay, Part I. London: J. B. Nichols and J. G. Nichols, 1848.
dg-rec-pt1.notes: Norman origins through Gerard de Gournay (G32). OCR quirks: Wilham/William (~6%), Basiha/Basilia (~16%). Page markers: ## p. N (#M) ## where N=book page. See sources/corpus/daniel-gurney-readme.md.

dg-rec-pt2.citation: Gurney, Daniel. The Record of the House of Gournay, Part II. London: J. B. Nichols and J. G. Nichols, 1848.
dg-rec-pt2.notes: Junior Norfolk Branch, West Barsham medieval Gurneys, through Henry G15. See sources/corpus/daniel-gurney-readme.md.

dg-rec-pt3.citation: Gurney, Daniel. The Record of the House of Gournay, Part III. London: J. B. Nichols and J. G. Nichols, 1848.
dg-rec-pt3.notes: Gurneys of Keswick: Francis G14 Merchant Taylor, Francis of Maldon, John of Norwich. Includes Appendix C (Court of Wards records, Merchant Taylors' Company membership). See sources/corpus/daniel-gurney-readme.md.

dg-rec-pt4.citation: Gurney, Daniel. The Record of the House of Gournay, Part IV: The Gournays of Somersetshire. London: J. B. Nichols and J. G. Nichols, c. 1848.
dg-rec-pt4.notes: Part IV main text = THE GOURNAYS OF SOMERSETSHIRE (pp. 593–703); ADDENDA (pp. 704–714); INDEX (pp. 715–722); LIST OF ILLUSTRATIONS (pp. 723–724). Normalized from Internet Archive OCR. See sources/corpus/daniel-gurney-readme.md for pagination grammar and section map.

dg-rec-supp.citation: Gurney, Daniel. The Record of the House of Gournay, Supplement. London: Priv. print., 1858.
dg-rec-supp.notes: Text extraction into corpus pending. Contains detailed notes supplementing all four parts.

dg-rye-appendix.citation: Rye, Walter. Appendix to Daniel Gurney's Record of the House of Gournay.
dg-rye-appendix.notes: Rye's additions to the Supplement. Distinct from rye-norfolk-antiquarian (Rye's separate 1893 article). Text extraction pending.

rye-norfolk-antiquarian.shortTitle: Rye, Norfolk Antiquarian — Gurneys of Norwich
rye-norfolk-antiquarian.citation: Rye, Walter. 'The Gurneys of Norwich.' The Norfolk Antiquarian Miscellany.
rye-norfolk-antiquarian.notes: Walter Rye's article on the Gurneys of Norwich. Critical for: (a) the multiple Gurney/Gurnell/Gurling/Garney name variants in Norwich registers, (b) plebeian Gurney lines in Norwich (shoemakers, cordwainers, lace weavers) from whom John the Quaker may have descended, (c) the disambiguation problem distinguishing related lines. Heavily relevant to John Gurney-1 research and the two-Francis problem.

three-hundred-years-norman-house.shortTitle: Hannay, Three Hundred Years of a Norman House
three-hundred-years-norman-house.citation: Hannay, James. Three Hundred Years of a Norman House: The Barons of Gournay from the Tenth to the Thirteenth Century. London: Tinsley Brothers, 1867.
three-hundred-years-norman-house.corpusPath: sources/corpus/threehundredyear00hann - THEEE HUNDRED YEAES OF A NORMAN HOUSE.txt
three-hundred-years-norman-house.notes: Independent Victorian secondary source on the Gournay barons (10th–13th c.), parallel to but not derived from Daniel Gurney. Useful for cross-checking DG's Norman-period claims (G37–G33) against a separate scholarly tradition. Title page typo on file: 'THEEE HUNDRED YEAES' = OCR misread of 'THREE HUNDRED YEARS.'

gournay-en-bray-1844.shortTitle: Supplément aux recherches historiques sur Gournay-en-Bray (1844)
gournay-en-bray-1844.citation: Supplément aux recherches historiques sur la ville de Gournay-en-Bray. 1844.
gournay-en-bray-1844.corpusPath: sources/corpus/Supplément aux recherches historiques sur la ville de Gournay-en-Bray 1844 with mentions about Daniel Gurney.txt
gournay-en-bray-1844.notes: French local history of Gournay-en-Bray, the Norman ancestral seat. Predates DG by 4 years; contains independent local-archive material on the seigneury and the Gournay/Gurney family. Notable: contains explicit mentions of Daniel Gurney (English correspondent), establishing transatlantic 19th-c. communication on the family history. Primary value: independent French perspective on the Norman seat (G37–G31).

nro-pd-12-1.shortTitle: NRO PD 12/1 (St Martin at Palace, Norwich)
nro-pd-12-1.citation: Parish register, St Martin at Palace, Norwich, 1538–1639. Norfolk Record Office, PD 12/1.
nro-pd-12-1.notes: BREAKTHROUGH SOURCE (March 2026): Francis Gurney + Margaret Rybett marriage, 23 September 1611. Image examined on Ancestry; paleographic reading confirmed.

nro-pd-86-41.citation: Parish register, East Dereham, Norfolk. Norfolk Record Office, PD 86/41 (microfilm, 69 images).
nro-pd-86-41.notes: Systematically reviewed. Five Francis Gurney baptisms identified (Entries A–E). Entry E: 'John son of [ffrancis Gurnie?]' — four-test paleographic analysis supports ffrancis over Nicholas. Margaret Rybett death revised to c.1616–17 based on 9-month impossibility test. Note: parish register image captures committed to sources/media/parish-register/ April 2026 (verify whether East Dereham or West Dereham — Allen's note used 'West Dereham' which may be a typo; the research has been East Dereham focused).

anderson-gmd-2015.citation: Anderson, Robert Charles. The Great Migration Directory: Immigrants to New England, 1620–1640: A Concise Compendium. Boston: NEHGS, 2015 (extract from p. 158 added April 2026 from 2025 reprint/edition).
anderson-gmd-2015.notes: John Gurney-1 entry. Assigns 'Unknown' English origin = implicit rejection of Banks's Bury St. Edmunds attribution under modern standards. Arrival date: 1636 — discrepancy with June 1641 Weymouth record; unresolved. Page 158 excerpt now in corpus (partial); full directory not extracted.

banks-brownell-1937.citation: Banks, Charles Edward. Topographical Dictionary of 2885 English Emigrants to New England, 1620–1650. Ed. Elijah Ellsworth Brownell. Philadelphia: Bertram Press, 1937.
banks-brownell-1937.notes: John Gurney-1 on p. 151 (Suffolk — Bury St. Edmunds). Source: 'Banks Mss.' only — no primary citation. East Anglian placement weakens Candidate A (Stewkley) more than Candidate B. Cluster analysis: surrounded by genuine BSE emigration group (Newgate, Chaplin, Knapp, Goodrich, Bright, Townsend, Atkinson, Cooke, Wright). Banks died before publication; Brownell edited. See validation file for full analysis.

blomefield-norfolk.citation: Blomefield, Francis. An Essay Towards a Topographical History of the County of Norfolk. 11 vols. London, 1805–1810.
blomefield-norfolk.notes: Key parish entries: Harpley (vol. viii, pp.452–459), West Barsham (vol. vii, pp.42–47), Great Ellingham (vol. ii). Independently confirms multiple DG pedigree points.

hop-gurney.citation: History of Parliament Trust. 'Sir John Gurney (d.1408).' The History of Parliament: the House of Commons. historyofparliamentonline.org.
hop-gurney.notes: Sir John Gurney d.1408 biography. Confirms collateral status: son Edmund died under age, estates to nephew Thomas (Robert's son). John of Gaunt stewardship to be verified here.

pease-pennyghael.citation: Pease, Howard. Gurney family genealogy. pennyghael.org.uk/Gurney.pdf.
pease-pennyghael.notes: Source of Ryvett claim for Francis G14's first wife. Confirmed against NRO PD 12/1 (March 2026).

burke-ancient-family.shortTitle: Burke, The Ancient Family of Gurney
burke-ancient-family.citation: Burke, J. Bernard. The Ancient Family of Gurney. Reprinted, Asbury Park, NJ: Martin & Allardyce.
burke-ancient-family.notes: Brief secondary heraldic-genealogical pamphlet. Arms: Argent, a cross engrailed gules, quartering Gournay, Warren, and Barclay. Crests: 1st on a chapeau gules turned up ermine, a fish in pale head downwards; 2nd a wrestling collar or. Seat: Keswick, near Norwich. Used for heraldic and family-context reference.

hingham-register.notes: Ann Gurney married John Gilman, 1 Oct 1626. Relationship to Francis G14's family unresolved.

brs-v21.citation: Buckinghamshire Record Society, vol. 21. 1642 Buckinghamshire tax records.

vch-bucks-v3.citation: Victoria County History: A History of the County of Buckingham, vol. 3.
vch-bucks-v3.notes: Stewkley manors. Used in Candidate A analysis.

freebmd-freereg.notes: FreeREG confirmed Francis G14 burial 9 Jan 1646/7, St Botolph Bishopsgate. Corrected Boyd's 1641 misread.

domesday-1086.notes: Hugh de Gournay III (G33): Liston, Fordham, Ardleigh (Essex); Norfolk properties. Referenced in DG-I.

tag-10-70.notes: TIER 1 PULL — highest priority. Not yet obtained. Content unknown but flagged as significant for John Gurney-1. Cited by Anderson (GMD p. 158) — almost certainly the source of his 1636 arrival date.

nehgr-62-94.citation: New England Historical and Genealogical Register, vol. 62, p. 94.
nehgr-62-94.notes: TIER 1 PULL — highest priority. Not yet obtained. Cited by Anderson (GMD p. 158) — likely contains earliest published discussion of John Gurney-1's origin.

nichols-herald-v3.citation: Nichols, John Gough, ed. The Herald and Genealogist, vol. 3. London: J. B. Nichols and Sons, 1866.
nichols-herald-v3.notes: p. 9: heraldic note on Barons of Gournay arms (plain sable shield), citing DG p. 19. Secondary citation endorsing Daniel Gurney's heraldic authority. Vol. 4 (1867) searched thoroughly — no Gurney/Gournay content (first-class negative). Vols. 1, 2, 5–8 not yet exhaustively searched.

heralds-visit-london-1633.citation: Heralds' Visitation of London, 1633. College of Arms, London. Certified copy by Charles George Young, York Herald, 4 May 1831.
heralds-visit-london-1633.notes: Francis G14's own attestation of his pedigree and children. Transcribed in DG-III-524. PRIMARY SOURCE for Francis as 'of London, merchant, living a'o 1634' and son of Henry Gurney of Great Ellingham.

heralds-visit-essex-1664.citation: Heralds' Visitation of Essex, 1664. College of Arms, London. Certified copy by Charles George Young, York Herald, 4 May 1831.
heralds-visit-essex-1664.notes: Francis Gurney of Maldon's own attestation. Transcribed in DG-III-537. John Gourney 'sonne and heire, aet. 9 a'o 1664' = born c.1655.

st-benet-fink-register.citation: Parish register, St Benet Fink, City of London. Baptisms 1619–1637.
st-benet-fink-register.notes: Children of Francis G14 + Anne Browning: Dorothy 1619, Roger 1621, Frances 1626 (d. same year), Francis 1628, Lucretia 1630, Thomas 1636, Margaret 1637. Transcribed DG-III-525.

st-mary-maldon-register.citation: Parish register, St Mary's, Maldon, Essex.
st-mary-maldon-register.notes: Birth/baptism of John Gourney, 7 Oct / 30 Oct 1655. Ten children of Francis Gurney of Maldon listed in DG-III-537.
